### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **71** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**39** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **74** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `decc16062cb351f460fc47edc8738876379c6e18` — the merge of head `7f68e294b5327c678ee0016915b8a610b0a4720f` into base `1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin decc16062cb351f460fc47edc8738876379c6e18 && git checkout decc16062cb351f460fc47edc8738876379c6e18
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1 7f68e294b5327c678ee0016915b8a610b0a4720f && git checkout -B drift-repro 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1 && git merge --no-ff 7f68e294b5327c678ee0016915b8a610b0a4720f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Scope: `.changeset/31699-webhook-names-per-namespace.md`, `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`, `packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts` (on `origin/main`), `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/upgrade-impact-report.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts`, `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts`

### ① Derived judgments
- **Touched suites at head (built with `OS_SKIP_DTS=1`):**
  - plugin-webhooks whole package 270/270;
  - runtime catalog-activation-door and meta-write-org-scope 98/98;
  - objectql e8 readers, ai-family, flow-family and ledger backfill 247/247;
  - core package-scoped-resolution 28/28;
  - metadata whole package 1402/1403. The one red is `typescript-serializer-annotation.test.ts` (TS7016), from the DTS-skipped build, not this PR;
  - cli Q4 ceremony 17/17;
  - dogfood flow-family, upgrade-18x, webhook-materialization and wall-declared-webhook 38/38.
- **Ten ablations, each red:**
  - R1, the subscription id without the package: 3 red.
  - R2, redelivery read by name: 1 red.
  - R3, `webhookSlotSwitch` ignoring the slot's own row: 8 red.
  - R4, an unowned row turning on holders under two slots: 1 red.
  - R5, the name guard reading ambiguity as "not taken": 1 red.
  - R6, the redelivery guard rethrowing the ambiguity: 1 red.
  - D1–D4, the door (back to name addressing, never adopting, adopting under two holders, picking the first co-owner): 2, 1, 1 and 1 red.

  So the dispatcher, the ledger, the redelivery guard, the name guard and the door are each pinned.
- **Claims verified:**
  - `webhook` is in all three sets (`package-scoped-resolution.ts:149`, `package-scoped-read.ts:115`, `package-slotted-store.ts:106`).
  - `POST /security/_activation/webhook/:ns/:name` is mounted (`dispatcher-plugin.ts:2262`) with its ledger row.
  - A package's declaration delivers under `declared:PKG/NAME`; the environment's own keeps `declared:NAME`.
  - Legacy `declared:NAME` rows are judged as before with one holder and refused naming both with two (pinned, ablation R6 red).
  - The CLI ceremony keeps `declared:NAME` (pin green).
  - `Skills-docs:` is true, and the changeset matches the body.
- **CI at the head (06:50Z):** 56 success, 12 skipped, **1 failure (`Test Core (1/8)`)**, 2 running.
- **Trial merges:**
  - `origin/main` 0f9b56539: clean, but semantically red (MF2).
  - #32497 (`phk4r9`): clean.
  - #32507 (`wqgmuu`): 8 conflict files.
  - #32513 (`du44hj`): 4 conflict files.
  - All of these conflicts are in the type sets, their doc and their tests.

### ② Semver level
- `minor` on five packages, with `!` and a BREAKING banner, matches PR 1 (#32214).
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is on the body and the changeset, with the same two answers. `Metadata-protocol: added` is correct.
- The banner's "One holder: every answer is as before except the `ref_id`" is false until MF3 is settled.

### ③ Boundary flags
- The diff stays inside the claimed surface, plus the two seat-approved files and the doc.
- `connectorNameRefusal` is out of scope (PR 3). `connector` stays outside the narrowed set, with its 422 CONTROL pinned.
- One reader of the class lives outside the diff: `plugin-security/src/upgrade-impact-report.ts` (S1).
- The semantic conflict with `main` sits in another card's test (#32548), see MF2.

### ④ Design judgment
**Must-fix**
1. **MF1: a disabled package's declared webhook is delivered when another namespace's package holds the same name.** Red line 1.
   - Where: `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/declared-webhooks.ts:291-303` (`slotsOf`). It reads holders, items and resolution on the raw registry from `packageScopedRegistryOf` (`:237-252`). Those raw reads count a disabled package, while the listing the name came from withholds it.
   - What moves: A is enabled, and B of another namespace is disabled, and both declare `NAME`.
     - FROM: unreachable (install answered 422), and a lone disabled holder is not dispatched.
     - TO: B's declaration is subscribed and delivered to B's URL with B's secret, and a redelivery of `declared:B/NAME` is allowed.
     - Also TO: the bare read is refused, naming the disabled holder, and a legacy `declared:NAME` delivery of A is refused, where `/meta` treats a disabled package as no holder.
   - Measured, unit (a real `SchemaRegistry`, `disablePackage(B)`): one event gives two deliveries, one to `/alpha` and one to `/beta`. CONTROL: B alone and disabled gives no delivery.
   - Measured, booted (flow-family dogfood stack): a disabled `kappa` stops delivering its own-name webhook but keeps delivering the shared one.
   - Fix:
     - Give `slotsOf` and the resolver a registry slice that withholds disabled holders, as `registry.ts:8949-8955` builds one.
     - Pin it in both registration orders, with CONTROLs: both enabled, and a lone disabled holder. Pin that re-enabling resumes delivery.
     - Settle `adoptPackageless` (`catalog-activation.ts:523`, `:563`) so it counts a disabled holder and never re-attributes a package-less "off" row to the enabled one.
     - Add the FROM → TO row.
2. **MF2: CI is red, `Test Core (1/8)`.**
   - Where: `packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts:106` meets `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts:2071` on `main` (0f9b56539, #32548).
   - That describe iterates every unbundled member of `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES` and expects the boot priming pass to register each one.
   - `webhook` has no row in `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY`, and the pass walks only that registry. So three cases fail (`:2158`, `:2199`, `:2222`).
   - Reproduced locally on the merge with `main`: 3 failed, 24 passed.
   - The seat rules the fix (ruling on #31699).
3. **MF3: an undeclared one-holder answer moves, and an event is lost.** Red line 3.
   - Where: `declared:PKG/NAME` (`auto-enqueuer.ts:593`, `declared-webhooks.ts:153-155`) is written as `ref_id`, capped at 128 (`http-delivery.object.ts:126`), and inside `dedup_key`, capped at 191 (`:133`).
   - What moves: with one holder, a long name that delivered before now fails the outbox insert, and the event is lost. It is logged once and reported nowhere else.
   - Measured, booted: a 101-character name gives `Ref ID must be ≤ 128 characters (got 129)` and the "event is LOST" line. On `main` its reference is 110 characters (computed, not run on `main`).

**Should-fix**
- **S1.** `plugin-security/src/upgrade-impact-report.ts` reads the webhook ledger and the declaring package by name.
  - `shippingPackage` (`:443-446`) and `shipper` (`:536-541`) take the first artifact of the name. So the report misses or under-names withheld webhooks under two holders.
  - Its remedies name the bare door (`:746`, `:785`), which answers 409 under two holders.
  - Read only, not run.
- **S2.** Two remedies point at a door that refuses: `redeliver-guard.ts:233-235` and `DeclaredWebhookNameConflictError` (`declared-webhooks.ts:593`) name `webhook/NAME` for a slot that names a package. Name the namespace address there instead.
- **S3.** `GET /meta/webhook/NAME/published` (`meta.ts:1556-1565`) shares narrowing (1). Name it in the row and pin it.

**Nits**
- `heldByRow` (`auto-enqueuer.ts:560-570`) is by name. That is the safe direction; say so in the module doc.
- The body's "CI on the PR: not read yet" is stale.

The narrowing itself is right against the spec on `main`. The three must-fixes are what stops it.

- **Red line 1 (resolution never loosened): broken.**
  - With one holder enabled and a second holder of the same name disabled, the disabled package's declared webhook is subscribed, delivered to its own URL, and allowed on redelivery.

    - the redelivery veto judges a named slot exactly (R2);

- **Red line 2 (ambiguity reported, never guessed): holds in the diff.**
  - The bare read, the bare door, the name guard and the redelivery veto each refuse a two-holder name naming both, each pinned.
  - A legacy `declared:NAME` delivery under two holders is refused and sent to neither.
  - Outside the diff, `plugin-security/src/upgrade-impact-report.ts` still takes the first package of a webhook name in a boot report. That is a guess in a report (should-fix S1).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `938f948b2c5e05938246e0bbdff89725ef02a243`
Local-runs: probe — own worktree at the head; touched suites plugin-webhooks 284/284, runtime 156/156, objectql 250/250, metadata 1432/1433 (the one red is `typescript-serializer-annotation.test.ts` TS7016 from a DTS-skipped build, as in round 1), plugin-security report 42/42, service-messaging 888/888, core 29/29, dogfood 38/38; single-change ablations (each restored), scratch probes in both registration orders, a booted three-holder probe; the head merged with main `c4b6160d21` built, touched suites and three gates re-run there
Scope: round-2 delta over FAIL records 6816920433 and 6816929999 and ruling 6816940784 (R2-A..D), plus a sweep of every webhook reader for served set versus every holder

### ① Derived judgments

**R2-A (a disabled package is no holder for what serves; a durable read counts every holder): met, with two gaps.**
- Booted with three holders, one disabled through the registry: only the enabled holder's event was delivered, and delivery resumed on re-enable. The served slots exclude the disabled package, and `holdersOf` lists all three.
- The activation door's bare address answers 409 naming the served holders only. The disabled package's namespace address answers 409 at the door and 404 on `/meta/webhook/NS/NAME`.
- Ablations that went red:
  - served holders unfiltered: 2 tests;
  - ledger ownership taken from the served set: 2;
  - `holdersOf` taken from the served set: 2;
  - the door's `adoptPackageless`, three variants: 1 each;
  - ledger addressing: 3.
- Gap 1 is the legacy redelivery case (M1). Gap 2 is the `GET /meta` bare read (M2).
- The branch at `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/declared-webhooks.ts:371` has no pin (M4).

**R2-B (stored webhook rows at boot): pins exist for the order-free cases only.**
- The three boot-hydration pins pass with the three type sets reverted, so they pin existing behaviour, as the dev says.
- The residual in Q1 reproduces in both registration orders:
  - a stored row naming no package, or naming a non-holder, lands in the first-registered holder's slot;
  - of two rows each naming a holder, only the last loaded applies.
- The census warning `metadata_sealed_overlay_unserved` fires for these rows, while the dispatcher does serve the first kind. The changeset says the opposite (M3).

**R2-C (delivery references): met at the per-record site, unpinned at the bulk site.**
- Ablations that went red:
  - `ref_id` back to 128: 1;
  - the `dedup_key` boundary: 1 on each side;
  - digest off at the per-record site (`auto-enqueuer.ts:1244`): 1.
- Digest off at the bulk-event site (`auto-enqueuer.ts:1401`) leaves 284/284 green (M4).

**R2-D (remedies name the namespace address) and the upgrade-impact report by (package, name): met.**
- Ablations that went red: the name-guard remedy (2), the redelivery remedy (1), the report's `ships` (1), the report's shippers (1).
- The report's `covered` by (package, name) stays green under two ablations (S2).

**CONTROL (one-holder answers unchanged): holds, except as declared.**
- The one-holder pins are green: the metadata boot-pass read, the boot-hydration control and the dogfood control.
- The only one-holder answer that moves is the new `ref_id` shape, declared as row (2).
- One undeclared condition sits on an un-migrated PostgreSQL or MySQL database (Q2, S3).

**Moved answers declared and pinned.**
- Row (1), from 200 first-registered to 409 naming both: declared. Its pin goes red when the type-set flip is reverted, where the read answers 200 with the first-registered declaration. The FROM is correct as written.
- Row (2): declared and pinned.
- The disabled co-holder bullet is declared, but its `GET /meta` clause is false (M2).
- The legacy redelivery answer is neither declared nor pinned (M1).

**Class sweep.**
- Readers on the served set, pinned: dispatch, the door's bare address, the name guard, and redelivery of a package-named reference.
- Readers on every holder, pinned: ledger row ownership, the unowned-row report, the door's `adoptPackageless`, and the boot backfill.
- Two readers are on the wrong side:
  - redelivery of a reference naming no package reads the served set, and should read every holder;
  - the protocol's generic by-name read reads every holder, where the changeset says the served set.

### ② Semver level

- `minor` on seven packages, with the breaking marker and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, is unchanged from round 1. The `ref_id` widening is additive.
- `check-adr-0087-registration` passes on the merged tree, including main's new #32649 rule. The changeset carries `Metadata-protocol: added`, which that rule does not refuse.
- No level change is needed: M1 to M3 change text and one guard, not the level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Schema change on a system object.** `sys_http_delivery.ref_id` goes from 128 to 384, which needs `os migrate apply` on an existing PostgreSQL or MySQL database (Q2).
- **Mixed versions.** No double enqueue across versions was found. Record events are in-process (the in-memory realtime adapter is the only one in the tree), so one node enqueues each write. This is from reading, not booted.
- **Not measured:** the dev's claim that an old node redelivering a new-shape row fails closed.
- **Class gap outside this PR.** The protocol's generic by-name read (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`) counts disabled holders for every package-scoped type except `action`. Measured the same for `email_template`. It needs its own card.
- **Size:** 33 files, +1566/−256 = 1822 changed lines.

### ④ Design judgment

**Must-fix**

- **M1. Legacy redelivery picks a holder.**
  - Where: `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/redeliver-guard.ts:213-216`. A reference that names no package is judged by `declaredWebhookNamed`, which reads the served set.
  - Measured in both orders:
    - two holders, one enabled and one disabled: a `declared:NAME` delivery is allowed;
    - both enabled: refused, naming both;
    - a lone disabled holder: refused.
  - The function's own doc says such a delivery "belongs to one of them, and nothing says which", and that is still true when one holder is disabled. A delivery row is a durable reference, so R2-A's "a durable read counts every holder" applies.
  - Fix: when the reference names no package, count `holdersOf(name)`, and with two or more, refuse naming each. Pin both orders, with controls for one enabled holder (allowed), a lone disabled holder (refused) and two enabled holders (refused).
- **M2. The changeset's `GET /meta` clause is false.**
  - `.changeset/31699-webhook-names-per-namespace.md:30` says the bare read `GET /meta` answers the enabled holder.
  - Measured in unit tests in both orders, and booted: `GET /meta/webhook/NAME` and `/published` answer 409 naming both holders, the disabled one included. A lone disabled holder answers 404.
  - The answer fails closed, so the code is safe; the text and R2-A's list are not met.
  - Fix: correct the sentence and the PR body's reader table, and take the class card from ③.
- **M3. The changeset's package-less row sentence is false after a restart.**
  - Line 23 says a package-less row over a name two packages hold "is no slot's and is not dispatched".
  - On the boot path, that row is grafted into the first-registered holder's slot and dispatched as that holder's.
  - The PR body's Q1 says this, but the changeset, which ships, says the reverse.
  - Fix: qualify the sentence to what boot does, and name the follow-up card (Q1).
- **M4. Two R2 branches have no pin.**
  - `declared-webhooks.ts:371`, the "every holder disabled, nothing served" branch. With it removed, all suites stay green, and a lone disabled holder's webhook that a metadata service lists is dispatched.
  - `auto-enqueuer.ts:1401`, the digest at the bulk-event site.
  - Fix: one test each.
- **M5. A false "measured on main".**
  - `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-qualified-item-read.test.ts:592-593` and the PR body's Q3 say main already answered 409 over a registry holding both items.
  - With the three sets reverted and dist rebuilt, the read answers 200 with the first-registered declaration, and the pin goes red.
  - The docblock contradicts Clause-② row (1) inside the same PR. Fix: correct the docblock and the body. A stale dist during the dev's measure is the likely cause.

**Should-fix**

- **S1. A departed co-holder's ledger row is read as the remaining holder's switch.**
  - In `webhookSlotSwitch`, `if (slots.length <= 1) return unowned.every(Boolean)` treats a row naming a non-holder package like a package-less row.
